To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the level and rate of urbanization have differential impacts on the physical and the mental health of urban residents.
the level of urbanization, the speed of urbanization, and the location of urbanization all have different and complex associations with the physical and mental well-being of current residents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of urbanization and population movement on individual health, and the mechanisms underlying these impacts, in urban China.
the impact of urbanization, as measured by the percentage of the population living in urban areas at the county level, on individual physical health.
how urbanization affects the health of residents in urban China.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
urbanization is a mixed bag for health, with its effects varying across the dimensions of urbanization, the type of health outcome, the type of migrant, and the level and speed of urban development.

urbanization, especially the speed of urbanization, had a positive impact on the physical health of urban residents in China, while urbanization, in particular the acceleration of urbanization, has a negative impact on the mental health of residents, and that the effect of urbanization on health is mediated by the level of urbanization.

while the absolute level of urbanisation at the county level has a negative effect on self-reported physical health of residents, the process of urbanisation has a positive impact on the physical health of residents in China.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
urbanization and its dynamics have both positive and negative effects on health.
we have developed an analytical framework to understand the impact of the process of urbanization and the location of urbanization on individual health outcomes.

the urbanization process in China is complex and dynamic, and the impact of urbanization on health varies by dimensions of urbanization, and that the impact of urban health on individual health is more complex and dynamic than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of urbanization, rather than the simple dichotomy between rural and urban, have important implications for health in urban China.
urbanization is not a monolithic phenomenon.
the process of urbanization, and not just the level, matters.
